course_name_original: Fuentes y Aprovechamiento de Energías Renovables
course_name_en: Sources and Utilization of Renewable Energies
prerequisites: It is highly recommended that students have passed the courses “Fluid Mechanics” and “Thermal Engineering” to have acquired the necessary skills to apply basic concepts in a technological field.
Knowledge of energy equation and head loss concepts.
Application of thermodynamic principles to thermal machines.
Steam, gas, combined, and refrigeration power cycles.
Basic mechanisms of heat transfer: conduction, convection, and radiation.

learning_outcomes.text: Evaluate solar, geothermal, and biomass potentials in geographical areas.
Apply technologies for the conversion of solar, geothermal, and biomass energy into electrical energy.
Perform basic design of low-temperature solar thermal and geothermal installations.
Analyze the technical and economic viability of solar, geothermal, and biomass installations.
Ability to evaluate available hydraulic and wind energy resources in a given environment.
Understanding of basic technologies and operating modes of hydraulic and wind energy utilization systems.
Ability to perform basic design and operation calculations and to solve issues related to hydraulic and wind energy utilization systems.
Ability to analyze the technical and economic viability of hydraulic and wind energy utilization installations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to hydroelectric energy. Types of hydraulic exploitations
Evaluation of hydraulic resources. Notions of hydrology and reservoir management
Hydraulic turbines: impulse and reaction turbines
Introduction to wind energy. Evaluation of wind resources
Wind turbine technology and wind farm planning
Concentrated solar power plants and solar tower plants
Organic Rankine Cycles for electricity generation with solar, geothermal, and biomass resources.
teaching_methods: Group learning with faculty during face-to-face hours
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if all established minimums are reached, the final grade is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.7 × (P1+P2)/2 + 0.3 × OA. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0 points. P1, P2 and OA refer to the two parts of the written exams and other activities, respectively. For the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain at least 4 out of 10 points in P1 and P2 (or both parts of the full exam if P1 was not passed). The grade obtained in OA does not require a minimum score. In the extraordinary call, the same elements and weights apply, with an obligatory minimum of 4 points out of 10 in both P1 and P2 parts of the final exam. If a student has not completed any complementary activities (OA), the maximum possible grade is 7 out of 10.
